canonical_owner: Halo-2-Decompiled multiplayer/master_server owns account authorization and room capabilities; this website repository retains the exact deployment patch and contract, alongside the existing trusted Rust EOS worker.
problem: Anonymous DeviceID identities are shared by ordinary clients in one OS namespace, so two accounts on one PC can be rejected as the same EOS transport user.

compatibility.mixed_groups: Never matched together; no silent downgrade
compatibility.descriptor_shape: Unchanged eos-p2p-v1 socket/peers/session metadata; v14 clients explicitly choose account login.

endpoints.authorization: Bearer of a current, live, verified physical room owner

response.token: Short-lived signed OpenID ID Token; stable private account subject supplied by server only

request.token: EOS Connect ID Token from the official SDK

security: Onlyv14 rooms accept these routes; v13 returns409 and retains its anonymous signaling behavior.
Guest seats have no room bearer and cannot choose a player UUID/PUID.
JWT sub is decoded only as a bounded untrusted routing hint for the existing official EOS VerifyIdToken worker. It confers no authorization.
Worker verifies expected OpenID provider, client, product, sandbox, deployment and PUID; returned verified master account must equal the bearer-derived physical owner.
Room object identity, closed/deadline state, physical owner and current bearer are revalidated after request body reads and SDK verification.
Existing immutable eos_players binding and first-bind publication outbox are reused; repeat proof does not advance publication revision.
V14 peer signals must match the room-local verified binding, and existing distinct/unchanged physical peer identity guards remain.

Issuer/proof share a120/minute owner bucket; pending32 bound remains; queue admission is bounded to2 seconds and the owned worker create/write/read operation to20 seconds. Queued refusal/cancellation cannot close another caller’s worker; owned cancellation retires the stream before unlocking.
No social/account session is created, replaced or revoked; no trusted credentials, OpenID mapping, issuer or key is added.
validation_limits: HTTP tests use the explicit official-worker verification boundary; no live player/production HTTP mutation or rollout is implied.
Actual SDK shared-namespace rejection and isolated-namespace acceptance are separate bounded source-pinned evidence in Halo-2-Decompiled analysis/eos-live-matchmaking-failure-20261023.
Native end-to-end account transport and playable two-client join require separate qualification.
